# 10. Static Website Architecture

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Define how static files, URLs, generated assets, fallbacks, and hosting behavior must work without server application code.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] A build-free or build-time-only architecture decision record.
- [ ] A public folder or deploy root containing only files intended for publication.
- [ ] An index page for every directory URL that should resolve cleanly.
- [ ] A 404 page with helpful recovery links and no broken assets.
- [ ] A robots.txt file and sitemap.xml file generated from the final URL set.
- [ ] A security headers template for hosts that support static header files or dashboard rules.
- [ ] A cache policy for HTML, CSS, JS, images, fonts, documents, and generated metadata files.
- [ ] A static fallback policy for forms, search, filtering, translations, and interactive features.

## Must Be True
- [ ] The site must run from static hosting without Node, PHP, database, server sessions, or hidden builder runtime.
- [ ] All public URLs must work after a clean deploy and direct browser refresh.
- [ ] Relative paths must work for nested pages or be intentionally absolute with the final domain.
- [ ] Generated files must be reproducible and never hand-edited without updating the source process.
- [ ] HTML pages must be cacheable but able to receive timely corrections when content changes.
- [ ] Static search, filtering, and routing must not block core content indexing.
- [ ] The architecture must allow migration between free/static hosts with limited changes.
- [ ] Error pages and redirects must not depend on proprietary features unless documented with a portable fallback.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check that every internal link, image, CSS, JS, font, document, and preload target resolves from deployed paths.
- [ ] Check that URLs are canonicalized for HTTPS, host, trailing slash, and index.html variants where hosting allows it.
- [ ] Check that generated sitemap URLs match the final production domain and canonical tags.
- [ ] Check that hidden source files, drafts, config files, and backups are excluded from deploy output.
- [ ] Check that service workers are absent unless there is a strong reason and full update strategy.
- [ ] Check that SPA-style routing is not used for ordinary content pages that should be crawlable.
- [ ] Check that large data files are paginated, chunked, or avoided on static pages.
- [ ] Check that all static host behavior is documented in portable terms.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid requiring a proprietary builder export to regenerate the site.
- [ ] Avoid deploying source maps, drafts, design files, local configs, and raw content exports unless intentionally public.
- [ ] Avoid hashless long-cache assets that cannot be invalidated.
- [ ] Avoid JavaScript-only page routing for premium business and SEO-critical pages.
- [ ] Avoid depending on host-specific redirects without documenting equivalent rules.
- [ ] Avoid storing form submissions or personal data in static repository files.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] A clean clone plus documented commands must reproduce the deployable site.
- [ ] The deploy output must be portable across common free static hosts.
- [ ] Core pages must be robust when opened directly, refreshed, shared, indexed, and archived.
- [ ] Architecture decisions must reduce operational risk after launch.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use the fix script to generate robots.txt, sitemap.xml, 404.html, security header templates, and basic privacy-support assets.
- [ ] Use audits to flag unpublished source files and broken static references.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Core static features work without a backend: real static pages, correct navigation, static-friendly forms, success/error states, 404, sitemap, robots, and simple deployment.
- [ ] Front-end enhancements for sticky header, mobile menu, dropdowns, accordions, tabs, sliders, filters, client-side search, theme/accessibility controls, and back-to-top work only where included.
- [ ] Resilience: critical navigation and content do not depend on fragile scripts, forms fail gracefully, images/videos/embeds have fallbacks, third-party scripts do not block content, and each page can stand alone.
- [ ] Clean static URL behavior, canonical URLs, direct page URLs, anchors, 404 recovery, redirects, and asset paths are tested locally and after deployment.
- [ ] Build-free risks are covered: repeated components, manual metadata, manual sitemap, image optimization, link QA, translation updates, and component consistency.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
